audit.why: Early Xerath-favoured (750 Q range vs 525 soldier reach), evens at first item, Azir takes over two-plus items as a scaling hypercarry. Content layer says this; full-layer chart carried a blanket Skill on all seven rows.
audit.corrected: Full-layer sides aligned to the packet/content chart.

audit.why: Spikes correct: levels 3-5 kill window, level 6 evening, first item even, late Azir. Lost Chapter and Luden's timings present.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers; Shifting Sands shield (absorbs burst) was flagged missing; dos/donts bodies were pasted trade lines.
audit.why: Azir E is 22s at rank 1 / 16s max and carries a shield, so committing burst into it wastes the window; Xerath E stun is 13s at rank 1 and is the only counter to the dash. Both Xerath Q and E are projectiles his kit cannot block; Azir R (250 range) is terrain that knocks back but cannot reach artillery range.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns rewritten with real numbers, shield noted, bullets rewritten to match their titles.

audit.why: Azir E 22s rank 1 is the lane's longest punishable cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shifting Sands shield absorbing Xerath's burst was never stated.

edits.before: Q from fog-of-war range on his every last-hit — level 1 Xerath is the longest gun in the lane. Mana is the only governor.
edits.after: Your 750-range Q outranges his 525 soldier reach — you tax every last-hit at level 1 and he cannot answer. Watch mana.

edits.before: W joins the pattern: Q-W on the slowed target is the chip combo that defines the next twenty minutes.
edits.after: W joins the kit: Q into W on the slowed target is free chip he still cannot trade back into at 525 range.

edits.before: E completes the kill kit: the stun into full rotation is real damage even now. Hold it for HIS aggression, not yours.
edits.after: E completes the kill kit: stun his E dash onto a soldier and the full rotation lands. Hold it for his commit, not chip.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — the artillery goes infinite. Poke the wave contact, the trade attempt, and the recall walk.
edits.after: Lost Chapter makes the poke free while his Q still costs 70+ mana on a 14s cooldown — chip every wave contact he takes.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane online — chipped targets anywhere in the lane's zip code are now finishable. Shove and snipe.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane finishes chipped targets from off-screen; his R is only 250-range disengage. Shove and snipe.

edits.before: Late Xerath wins fights from the next postal code: stun the entry, barrage the objective, and never be seen.
edits.after: Two-plus items his stacked soldiers match your range with sustained DPS, and his R walls fights you must skip.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Shocking Orb for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — a shield-dash on a 22s cooldown at rank 1 (16s max); the shield eats your burst, so commit only after he burns it. - Your E stun is 13s at rank 1 — budget it for his dash, never for chip.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: After your Q lands or forces a sidestep, place W on the space he dodges into — the centre slow guarantees the follow-up hit.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: Overextended past river you are a short walk from his 1100-range E — the shield-dash starts fights you cannot end without Flash.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Azir wins by scaling: stacked soldiers eventually match your range, and Emperor's Divide walls off your escape.

Shifting Sands shield-absorbs-burst missing interaction folded into breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2].d. report[] left alone except none needed.
